_format: Slice 10b ts-js-framework ground truth. Written BEFORE the resolver, as in 5d-ii, 9a, 9b and 10a. Where the implementation and this file disagree, this file is the claim to argue against.
_endpoint: `address` is the entity name, which is what FTS5 tokenises. `path` is the DECLARED path: no prefix from `app.use("/v1", router)` is composed in, because that is a fact in another statement — and often another file — and a wrong URL is worse than a partial one.
_forbidden: Endpoints that must NEVER exist. Each is a specific wrong answer a plausible implementation would produce. Checked BEFORE set equality, because Slice 9a found a forbidden list behind set equality is unreachable and never fires.

forbidden.why: A router mount prefix composed into the declared path. `app.use("/v1", router)` is a separate statement and this fixture does not even contain it.
`cache` is `new Cache()`, not an Express application. Matching the call's spelling finds this.
A local class literally named Router is still not express.Router.
An object literal with a `get` property.
`Map.prototype.get` with one argument. A one-argument call is not a registration.
`app.all` is not an HTTP method. Expanding it into eight endpoints would assert eight declarations where the source made one.
`PREFIX + "/items"` evaluated. Nerve does not evaluate expressions.
An inline arrow function has no entity, so there is no target for the edge.
`handlers.list` is a member expression, not a locally declared name.
`Views.handle` is a member expression. It IS a declared static method, but resolving it means resolving the receiver first, which this rule does not do — see known_false_negatives.
`app` is imported from another module. Emitting this needs cross-module value tracking, the stated lower bound.

_unsupported_by_form: Every construct Nerve read and declined, counted by form. The gate asserts this map exactly, so a new unreadable form cannot appear silently and the precision denominator stays auditable. Same three forms 10a uses; `methods-not-literal` is Flask-specific and correctly absent.
_ambiguous: Declarations the source really does make twice. Both edges are kept; the ambiguity is reported rather than resolved by choosing one.
_known_false_negatives: Routes a human can see and Nerve does not record. Asserted ABSENT, so an FN cannot be quietly 'fixed' by a guess — promoting one has to be a deliberate change to this file.

known_false_negatives.reason: app-not-local: the binding proving `app` is an Express app is in routes.ts.
path-not-literal: evaluating `PREFIX + "/items"` is expression evaluation, and recording the operand text would be a guess at the address.
handler-not-a-symbol: an inline arrow is a callable with no entity, so no target exists.
handler-not-a-symbol: `handlers.list` names a property, not a declared symbol.

handler-not-a-symbol: `Views.handle` is a real static method, and this is the most defensible FN in the set. Resolving it needs the receiver resolved first; the Python rule declines the same shape, and doing it on one language only would make the relation mean different things per language.

_not_a_route: Symbols that must have NO incoming SERVED_BY edge. A control against a rule that attaches endpoints too eagerly.
_gates: 1. Every entry in `resolved` exists, with exactly the stated address, handler and handler kind.
2. No entry in `forbidden` exists. Checked FIRST.
3. Nothing in `not_a_route` has an incoming SERVED_BY edge.
6. FP = 0 and FN = 0 beyond the declared ones.
7. Express is reported as its OWN table, never summed with FastAPI or Flask.
8. Every SERVED_BY observation carries FRAMEWORK_RULE / DIRECT and extractor id ts-js-framework.
9. No ts-js-framework observation carries a relation other than SERVED_BY, asserted over Relation::ALL.
10. negative.ts contributes zero endpoints AND zero unsupported counts.
11. Zero py-framework observations in a repository with no Python — the 5d-i invariant, restated.
